acceptance: CI on the library runs the TPC-H corpus replay on every PR and fails on any parameter mismatch; the pinned BenchBox commit is visible in the workflow.
The two seed-0 cases (Q7, Q12) are asserted to raise the documented non-termination error.
All 10,000 random-seed cleaned-text digests match in a BenchBox test that calls the library.
`-p` is either implemented with corpus cases or rejected with a tested error.
description:
## Problem
Library draft PR #6 (TPC-H qgen) passes the corpus locally (1,958/1,960 named cases; 230,000/230,000 random-seed parameter lists) but its Rust and Python corpus tests skip unless BENCHBOX_CHECKOUT is set, so CI does not run them. Cleaned-text digests are checked for only the first 500 of 10,000 random seeds in Python because `_clean_sql` lives in BenchBox. `-p` stream permutation numbering is not implemented and has no corpus coverage. The full library test suites and the licence check were not run locally on that branch.

## Change
Add a CI job that fetches BenchBox's corpus and templates at a pinned BenchBox commit (no TPC text committed to the library) and runs the corpus tests; verify all 10,000 random-seed text digests in the BenchBox-side integration tests where `_clean_sql` lives; decide `-p` handling.

## Decision gates
- If fetching TPC templates in public CI raises a licence concern, stop and ask the owner (see datagen-decision-tpc-derived-code-licensing).
- `-p`: implement only if BenchBox uses qgen's own stream permutation; BenchBox computes TPC-H stream order in Python today, so the default is to document it as unsupported and raise a clear error.

## Guardrails
- BenchBox work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, make agent-write-preflight); the primary clone is read-only.
- Heavy work only through make heavy-run; never bypass or signal the lock, and never kill processes by name pattern (pkill -f); stop only PIDs you started.
- Commits as the configured human identity; no agent attribution.
- No carried or own reimplementation of upstream code without the owner decision recorded in datagen-decision-upstream-gap-policy.
- A choice between a small and a large implementation path goes to the owner with sizes before work starts.
- Report only results that were observed; name anything not run.
